newsitem.title: YEMEN: EU plans to grant Yemen $65 million in aid.
newsitem.headline: EU plans to grant Yemen $65 million in aid.

text.p: The European Union said on Sunday it planned to grant the impoverished Arab state of Yemen about $65 million in aid over the next two years.

"The European Union envisages that its overall aid for Yemen during the period between 1996 and 1998 could amount to approximately $65 million," said Michael Kohler, the European Union's desk officer for Yemen.
"This aid will take the form of projects and food security assistance," Kohlar, who is in Yemen as part of an EU delegation, told a news conference in Sanaa.
He said the European Union had granted Yemen some $70 million in aid to date.
Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest states, is currently implementing the second phase of wide economic reforms agreed with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

The country forecast a 1996 budget deficit of 181.41 billion rials ($1.39 billion). Yemen's Deputy Prime Minister Mohammad Said al-Attar went to Paris last week for talks with the Paris Club of creditor nations on rescheduling 60 percent of its $8.2 billion debt.

The head of the EU delegation visiting Yemen, Eberhard Rhein, encouraged Yemen to join the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), which groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.

"The European Union is willing to help Yemen by talking to the GCC countries, and it is up to Yemen to move in this direction," said Rhein, who is responsible for EU policies in the Middle East and North Africa.

Yemen has repeatedly voiced interest in joining the regional alliance. But ties with GCC states, especially Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, were damaged by Sanaa's sympathy with Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990. Relations with Saudi Arabia have improved, but strains persist with Kuwait.
